title: Prioritise the work and build a roadmap
summary: You will always have more ideas than time. A simple, shared way of scoring them helps you choose, explain your choices and turn them into a roadmap the team and stakeholders can follow.

beginner: List every candidate piece of work in one place: features, fixes, research and technical work. Write each one as an outcome where you can.
Pick one scoring method and explain it to the team. RICE is a good start: Reach (how many people), Impact (how much it helps each), Confidence (how sure you are) and Effort (how much work).
Score each item with the team. Ask engineers for effort, and use your research and data for reach and impact. Lower the confidence score where you are guessing.
Sort by score, then sense-check the order. Move items for real reasons, such as deadlines, dependencies or legal duties, and write down why.
Group the top items into a roadmap with three columns: Now, Next and Later. Avoid exact dates beyond the next few weeks.
Share the roadmap with stakeholders, explain how you scored it, and agree how often you will revisit it (for example monthly).
intermediate: Gather all candidate work as outcomes, including technical and research work.
Score it with a shared method (RICE or similar), using real effort estimates and confidence levels.
Adjust for dependencies and fixed deadlines, and record each reason.
Publish a Now / Next / Later roadmap and set a review rhythm.
experienced: Keep one backlog of outcomes, with an agreed, visible scoring method.
Get effort estimates from engineering, and let confidence reflect the evidence.
Justify overrides in writing, and map dependencies.
Publish a Now / Next / Later roadmap, with a review date set.

canDelegateTo.task: Map dependencies and run the scoring session
Provide effort estimates and flag technical risks
Keep the backlog tidy and write each item as an outcome

toolExamples.jira: Add Reach, Impact, Confidence and Effort as custom number fields on epics, so you can sort and filter by score. Use Jira's timeline view for the Now / Next / Later roadmap.
toolExamples.azure-devops: Use the Effort and Value fields on features, and show the roadmap on a delivery plan.
toolExamples.linear: Use projects for roadmap items and priority labels for the scored order.
toolExamples.google-docs: If you have no tracker, a shared spreadsheet with one row per item and a RICE formula column works well.
toolExamples.miro: Run the scoring session live on a 2x2 grid (impact against effort) before you put numbers on it.
toolExamples.claude: Paste your scored list and ask which scores look inconsistent with each other, and what questions a sceptical stakeholder would ask.

definitionOfDone: All candidate work scored with a method the team understands
Every change to the scored order has a written reason
Now / Next / Later roadmap shared with stakeholders
pitfalls: Scoring alone, so the team does not trust the result
Treating the score as the final answer rather than a starting point
Putting firm dates on items months away
